refNota: Use the attached image as the reference for the person and for the local. SAME shop assistant: Mexican woman in her late twenties, the same face, the same eyebrows, the same features, the same warm brown skin, the same dark hair pulled into the same low bun, the same small silver stud earrings, the same plain black crew-neck t-shirt, the same soft yellow measuring tape hanging around her neck. SAME LOCAL, element by element: the same small lingerie stall inside a Mexican covered market, the same back wall covered from waist height to the ceiling with bras on slim black hangers, the same glass display case with sliding doors on the left holding sealed three-packs, the same green painted wall on the right with the same metal rolling shutter pushed up, the same low wooden counter with the laminate top across the front of the frame, the same tile floor, the same bare fluorescent tube overhead mixed with daylight from the market aisle. SAME CAMERA: the same eye-level 35 mm shot from the same position and the same distance, the same white balance, the same framing, with her standing behind the counter in the same spot of the frame as in the reference, at the same three-quarter angle, framed from the waist up with the same space above her head and the counter in the foreground.
escena: Same woman, same clothes, same market stall, same camera and same framing as the attached reference photograph — only her mood and the order of the place have changed. She now stands behind the same wooden counter, in the same spot, relaxed and smiling, holding a tablet in BOTH of her complete hands, close to her own body at counter height, the screen on and angled toward the camera showing a grid of colored squares with two cells highlighted and a short list of rows with colored status dots. ELEMENT BY ELEMENT, EVERYTHING STAYS AND ONLY GETS TIDY: the same bra wall behind her, now ordered — every hanger facing the same way, the garments grouped in clean rows by cup and band, plain colored size discs spaced evenly along the rails, and the scraps of paper that were taped to the rail are gone; the same glass display case on the left, its sealed three-packs now aligned in even rows behind the sliding doors; the same green painted wall and the same rolling shutter pushed up on the right; the same laminate counter, now wiped clear — the worn paper notebook is closed and pushed to the far corner, the loose paper slips, the tape roll, the mug and the calculator are gone, and only a small card terminal and a squared stack of clear polybags remain; the same tile floor, now clear, the cardboard boxes flattened and stacked neatly under the counter instead of blocking the space; the same bare fluorescent tube, with warm daylight from the market aisle. EXACTLY ONE PERSON IS IN THE FRAME — no customer, no second employee, no partial figure and no hand, arm, shoulder or fragment of any other body anywhere in the image: every hand visible is one of her own two hands, each clearly attached to her own arm and shoulder. IT IS STILL THE SAME MARKET STALL: it must not become a clean boutique, it must not gain wooden hangers, white walls, marble, spotlights or a designer interior, and no piece of furniture appears that was not in the reference. Calm and in control. DIGNITY RULE (the most important rule of this set, must be obeyed literally): NO PERSON IN UNDERWEAR ANYWHERE IN THE IMAGE, and NO PRINTED, PACKAGED OR DISPLAYED IMAGE INSIDE THE FRAME MAY SHOW A PERSON IN UNDERWEAR OR ANY UNCOVERED BODY — not on a catalog, a brochure, a poster, a banner, a wall print, a hanger card, a price tag, a box, a polybag, a wrapper, a shopping bag, a calendar or any screen. Catalogs, brochures and printed booklets appear only CLOSED, stacked flat or standing on edge showing their spine, and their covers are PLAIN AND BLANK in one solid color with no photograph, no illustration of a body and no text; never a catalog open on a page, never a spread with a photograph, never a blurred page that suggests a body. Anything printed that refers to product is a technical line drawing of a garment outline, a strip of fabric color swatches or plain color chips — never a photograph of a person. Every garment is on a hanger, inside a clear bag, inside a box or neatly folded, and NOBODY IS WEARING ONE: no mannequin, no dress form and no torso form wears lingerie, there are no bare torsos and no bare shoulders in the image. Customers and employees are Mexican people fully and modestly dressed in ordinary everyday clothes — t-shirts, blouses, sweaters, jeans — standing on the sales floor or at the counter, never inside a fitting room, never behind a fitting-room curtain, never next to an open fitting room; all fitting-room curtains in frame are fully closed and no one is entering or leaving them. No black censor bars anywhere. FRAMING RULE: never center, fill or crop the frame on anybody's chest or torso. People are photographed at a three-quarter angle, framed from the waist up with generous space and headroom, or with the merchandise in the foreground and the person standing behind it; the camera is at eye level looking level or slightly down, never at chest height, never a close-up of a person's body. Faces and hands are what read, never a torso. HANDS AND BODIES: every hand is complete and anatomically correct with five separate well-formed fingers and visible nails, no fused, melted or mitten-like hands, no overlapping fingers merging into each other; every arm belongs to a person fully visible in the frame, is of natural length and is clearly attached to that person's own shoulder — no floating or orphan hands, no hand entering from a frame edge without a visible body, no third hand, no extra limbs, no stretched rubbery arms, no impossible elbows; nobody reaches across the frame for anything; it is visually obvious who is holding each object. NOTHING FLOATS: every laptop, tablet, phone, box, bag and clipboard rests flat on a real table, shelf or counter, or is held in two complete visible hands — nothing hovers in mid air; every garment hangs from a hanger that is hooked on a rail, or lies folded in a bag, box or stack, never suspended by itself. NO TEXT: no readable text, letters or numbers anywhere in the image — not on tags, labels, boxes, bags, stickers, notebooks, catalog covers, price cards, packaging or signage; no logos, no brand marks, no QR codes, no barcodes; size tags and dividers are plain colored discs or plain colored stickers with no digits; every screen is ON, clearly visible and facing the camera showing abstract interface only — a grid of colored squares with one or two cells highlighted, rows with small round avatars and colored status dots, colored progress bars, small garment thumbnails, soft grey placeholder lines, color chips — never words, never numbers, never a grey or switched-off screen, never the back of the device. MEXICAN LINGERIE IDENTITY: unmistakably an ordinary Mexican neighborhood lingerie shop or a Mexican lingerie wholesaler, not an international chain and not a luxury flagship — a street-level or market local with a painted wall, tile floor, a wrought-iron security grille or a rolling steel shutter, bras hung close together on slim black hangers sorted by band and cup, plain colored size discs on the rails, a small counter with a card terminal, a spinner of bra extenders and clear straps, sealed three-packs of socks and panties, clear polybags with folded garments, cardboard boxes stacked on the floor, Mexican people of everyday build and everyday clothes; never a minimalist designer boutique, never a marble flagship, never a warehouse price club with blue racks and forklift pallets. Editorial documentary photography, 35 mm, real Mexican people working, natural light mixed with warm store light, photorealistic, shallow depth of field, not a 3D render, not an illustration.
